title: Multi-Source Research Agent
summary: Plan-execute coordinator fans out to isolated, read-only source workers, stores each source once by ID, then verifies every claim. Unsupported claims go to a human, never shown as verified.
autonomy: Level: bounded agent (Ch1, Ch24). The model plans sub-queries and writes prose; code enforces the plan check, budgets, read-only tools, deterministic merge and claim verification. No write actions on the outside world.

layers.name: Sources via MCP
layers.boundary_below: retrieved content is data, not instructions

nodes.label: Evidence store
nodes.note: each source stored once, by ID

nodes.label: Synthesizer
nodes.note: every claim cites a source ID

key_decisions: Orchestrator-workers, justified by parallel sources and context isolation (Ch31, Ch32)
Plan-execute with a code plan check, ReAct inside each worker (Ch13)
Every source stored once with an ID; citations can only point to it (Ch15, Ch35)
Verification is its own step; failure means review, not a softer answer (Ch15)
All tools read-only; web and paper text is untrusted data (Ch47)
No A2A: workers are in-process, so a protocol adds nothing (Ch62)
rationale: Single vs multi-agent: four independent sources are a legitimate reason to split (parallelism and context isolation); a supervisor-style coordinator keeps validation and accountability central (Ch31, Ch32).
Planning: plan-execute makes sequencing and coverage checkable in code before spending budget; workers use ReAct for adaptive search inside a step cap (Ch13, Ch7).
Shared state: each worker writes only its own artifacts; the coordinator merges by stable source ID, so completion order never changes the result (Ch33).
Grounding: hybrid retrieval for internal docs; similarity is a ranking signal, not proof, so the verifier checks each claim against stored evidence (Ch17, Ch16).
Protocols: MCP for the four source integrations; A2A only if a worker becomes a separately owned remote agent (Ch26, Ch34, Ch62).
Memory: none across runs in v1; the evidence store is per-run state. Add approved procedural memory (good sources per topic) later (Ch18).
trust_boundaries: User to brief: vague requests produce clarifying questions, never invented scope (Ch7, Ch10).
Source results to workers: bounded, truncated and labelled untrusted; embedded instructions are ignored and logged (Ch29, Ch47).
Workers to coordinator: typed artifact messages; malformed messages rejected, not interpreted (Ch33).
Draft to report: the claim verifier is the only path to 'verified' (Ch15, Ch44).
failure_handling: Per-worker step budget and timeout; a failed worker returns a typed failure and the report lists the gap instead of fabricating (Ch14, Ch35).
Global budgets with named stop reasons: MODEL_ANSWER, STEP_BUDGET, TOKEN_BUDGET, DEADLINE (Ch14, Ch52).
Idempotent source capture: re-fetching the same URL or doc ID does not duplicate evidence (Ch15).
Hop budget in the coordinator turns runaway delegation into a bounded failure (Ch32).
hitl: Brief approval when scope is ambiguous or the budget is large (Ch10).
Human review for unsupported, conflicting or low-similarity claims before they reach the report (Ch15, Ch44).
evals: Golden question set with expected source IDs, including unanswerable questions that must abstain (Ch41, Ch42).
Replay stored tool arguments without model calls to test determinism (Ch15).
Model judge only for synthesis quality, calibrated against human labels; deterministic checks for citations (Ch44).
Track cost and latency per run with quality; the slowest worker sets latency (Ch52).
risks: Indirect prompt injection from web pages: read-only tools, untrusted labels, no exfiltration route; owner: platform lead (Ch47).
Citation laundering (claim cites a source that does not support it): claim-level verifier plus sampled human audit (Ch15, Ch44).
Cost blow-up from fan-out: budget guard and per-worker caps (Ch52).
